title: The Geometra of Gravere: Two Parliaments, an Opera House, and a Hallway on Rodriguez Pena
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Gravere, and the Brother Who Raised Him

stops.name: Gravere, birth in the Val di Susa
stops.date_confidence: attested: the Regional Museum of Piedmontese Emigration gives 2 April 1860 at Gravere; Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997) give only 'nace en 1860 en Gravere de Susa'. Later summaries loosely write Susa. The family story that his mother died bearing him is not in either source and is left unconfirmed. Coordinates corrected to the village centre per Nominatim.
stops.campa: A son is born at Gravere, a stone village on the road that climbs the Val di Susa toward the French passes, in the year before Piedmont becomes the spine of a kingdom called Italy. His father is Giovanni Battista Meano, a notary. His mother is Susanna Favretto. The valley he is born into sends its sons out along that road every season, to Lyon, to Marseille, to America, and counts them when they come back. This one will go farther than most and will never be counted back in. The registers give the name Vittorio.
suggested_refs: The parish and civil registers of Gravere, Val di Susa, for April 1860
sources: Museo Regionale dell'Emigrazione Piemontese, museoemigrazionepiemontese.it/vittorio-meano/
Victoria Baeza, Rita Molinos and Mario Sabugo, Vittorio Meano, Cuaderno de Critica no. 77 (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 3

stops.name: Venaus, the notary's house and the early loss
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The 1997 study says only 'huerfano desde muy pequeno' and does not date the father's death; the association of Giovanni Battista Meano with Venaus and with a locally prominent Piedmontese family reaches this file through the same study, whose PDF the gathering pass could not open. The date orders the segment only.
stops.campa: The father's house stands at Venaus, further up the same valley under the Rocciamelone. Giovanni Battista Meano remarries and then dies while his youngest son is still small. What the record keeps of it is a single clause: orphaned very young. The boy passes to a stepmother and to his elder brother Cesare, an engineer, who takes charge of his schooling and will later take charge of his employment. No reachable document gives the year of the notary's death, or says what became of his practice.
suggested_refs: Notarial records of the Val di Susa for the practice of Giovanni Battista Meano
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 3

stops.name: Pinerolo, the title of geometra
stops.date_confidence: contested. Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997) place his schooling at the instituto, escuela tecnica and gimnasio of Pinerolo, and es.wikipedia agrees, giving 1878 for the diploma. The Museo Regionale dell'Emigrazione Piemontese, an attested source for his birth, says instead that he attended the technical schools of Turin. The two accounts are recorded, not reconciled.
stops.campa: At the institute, technical school and ginnasio of Pinerolo, on the plain below the Waldensian valleys, he takes the title of geometra: surveyor, measurer, the practical grade of Italian building. It is not an architect's title, and he will design two national parliaments on the strength of it. The Buenos Aires press will reach for the fact when the bills on the second one come due. He is eighteen, reportedly first in his class, and the Chamber of Commerce and Arts of Turin sends him a distinction worth three hundred lire.
suggested_refs: Registers of the Istituto Tecnico of Pinerolo for the class of 1878
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 3
es.wikipedia, 'Victor Meano'
Museo Regionale dell'Emigrazione Piemontese (contradicting: Turin)

stops.name: Turin, the Accademia Albertina and what cannot be proved
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Petriella and Cutolo have him studying architecture at the Accademia Albertina; the 1997 archival study repeats this only as 'segun algunos autores' and flags it as unconfirmed by primary documentation. No diploma, matriculation or graduation record was located. The date orders the segment.
stops.campa: Some authors send him from Pinerolo to the Accademia Albertina, Turin's academy of fine arts, for architecture. The archival study that has read the papers repeats the claim in the weakest form available to it: according to some authors, with no register behind it. No matriculation sheet has been found, and no diploma. He is in Turin in these years, and the drawing he does there is good enough to travel. Did the man who will build the Argentine Congress ever hold a qualification in architecture? The literature does not know.
suggested_refs: Matriculation registers of the Accademia Albertina di Belle Arti, Turin, 1878-1884
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 3, citing Petriella and Cutolo

stops.name: Turin, the drawings on Cesare's boards
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The office years and the excursions among Turin's monuments rest on Eugenio Ollivero's recollection of 1904, quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 3; the same recollection is the sole authority for Tamburini having recruited Meano on the strength of his drawings alone. Month is an ordering device.
stops.campa: In Cesare's engineering office he draws for a living, roads and water and calculation, at a board beside his schoolmate Eugenio Ollivero, who remembers twenty years later the excursions the two of them made through the porticoes and the baroque of the city. Into this room comes Francesco Tamburini, architect to the Argentine state, home from Buenos Aires and looking for hands. He offers the young geometra a place in a studio on the other side of the Atlantic. By Ollivero's account the whole basis of the offer is what is pinned to the board: he had seen, appreciated and praised the drawings.
stops.quote_source: Eugenio Ollivero (1904), on why Tamburini summoned Meano to Argentina, quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 3
suggested_refs: Eugenio Ollivero's address to the Collegio dei Geometri of Turin province, 30 June 1904, the source for the Turin years
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 3
working/journeys/francesco_tamburini.journey.json

stops.name: Genoa, the passage south
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The 1884 departure and the autumn arrival are attested in the 1997 study and confirmed by es.wikipedia and it.wikipedia. Genoa is inferred from the standard Piedmontese emigration route and no manifest was located. The report that the pair boarded under the name 'Mehan' and as husband and wife comes from the same study and is unverified.
stops.campa: He is twenty-four when he goes down to the sea at Genoa, the port through which Piedmont empties itself into the Americas. He does not go alone. Luigia Fraschini leaves a husband behind in Italy to go with him, and the account that has come down says the two of them signed the passenger list under a slurred version of his name and called themselves married, so that anyone who came looking would have nothing to follow. No manifest confirming it has been found.
suggested_refs: Passenger lists of the Genoa to Buenos Aires steamers, autumn 1884
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 3
es.wikipedia, 'Victor Meano'
it.wikipedia, 'Vittorio Meano'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the landing at the Aduana
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year: 1884 is confirmed by Anguita and Cecchini (Infobae, 2020), es.wikipedia and it.wikipedia, and the frequently repeated 1886 arrival is weaker. The exact day and the vessel are unknown, and the pin is the old customs house quarter rather than a documented berth.
stops.campa: The city he steps into is pulling down its colonial self at speed. Francesco Tamburini is architect to the national government, with the presidential house, the theatre, the hospitals and the police headquarters on his boards at once, and he needs draughtsmen who can carry a project through. Meano reaches that studio in the autumn of 1884 with a surveyor's diploma and no Spanish, and with a woman he cannot introduce as his wife. He never sees Italy again.
suggested_refs: The Paseo de Julio and the old Aduana, landing ground of the Italian emigration of the 1880s
sources: Alberto Anguita and Daniel Cecchini, 'El tragico final del arquitecto...', Infobae, 19 July 2020
Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 3
working/journeys/francesco_tamburini.journey.json

stops.name: Cerrito 680, the first rooms
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the address comes from Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), through a PDF the gathering pass could not read. Nominatim places Cerrito 680 in San Nicolas, one block from Cerrito 628, the ground later chosen for the new Teatro Colon. The date orders the segment.
stops.campa: They take rooms at Cerrito 680, in the low grid west of the Plaza, and keep to themselves. A couple who cannot produce a marriage certificate does not enter the salons of Buenos Aires, and the record of these years holds no dinners, no clubs and no patrons. It holds drawings. One block along the same street is a piece of open ground where the city intends, when it can afford it, to build itself a proper opera house. He passes the empty lot on his way to the studio every morning for six years.
suggested_refs: Cerrito 680, San Nicolas, one block east of the future Teatro Colon
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997)

stops.name: Casa Rosada, a government house of another man's design
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, downgraded here from the dossier's attested tag. Infobae (2020) puts the young Meano on Tamburini's state works including the Casa Rosada, but the building's official history at casarosada.gob.ar and es.wikipedia credit only Kihlberg, Aberg and Tamburini and never mention Meano. No room, facade or detail can be assigned to him.
stops.campa: Tamburini is joining two separate buildings into one government house, throwing the great central arch across Balcarce so that the pink mass reads as a single palace. Somewhere in that campaign a junior hand from the Val di Susa is drawing. Which sheets are his, nobody can say. The official history of the house names Kihlberg, Aberg and Tamburini and stops there, and the account that puts the young Italian on the state works assigns him neither a room nor a facade of his own.
suggested_refs: The Casa Rosada's official building history, which names Kihlberg, Aberg and Tamburini and no assistants
sources: Anguita and Cecchini, Infobae, 19 July 2020
casarosada.gob.ar/la-casa-rosada/historia (negative: no Meano)
working/journeys/juan_antonio_buschiazzo.journey.json

stops.name: Moreno 1550, the police headquarters that changes architects
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for Meano's part. The Tamburini project of June 1886 and the handoff from Juan Antonio Buschiazzo are attested in the atlas file for Tamburini; Meano's own hand in the work is reported only by Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), through a PDF the gathering pass could not read, and no element of the building is assigned to him.
stops.campa: The Central Police Department at Moreno 1550 begins as Juan Antonio Buschiazzo's design and passes to Tamburini's office to be finished, which is how work moves in this city: a public building changes architects the way a house changes tenants. Meano is at a board in that office through the handover of June 1886, watching a large work outlive the man who signed its first sheet. Four years later the Colon will change hands the same way over Tamburini's body, and he will be the one taking it up. The handover here is documented; his own part in the drawing is not.
suggested_refs: The Departamento Central de Policia at Moreno 1550, begun by Buschiazzo and completed from Tamburini's office
sources: working/journeys/francesco_tamburini.journey.json (stop 'Moreno 1550: the police headquarters taken over', 1886-06)
Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997)

stops.name: Cerrito 628, the cornerstone of the new Colon
stops.date_confidence: attested: the Teatro Colon's official history gives 25 May 1890 for the cornerstone and states the intention to open on 12 October 1892, the Columbus quadricentennial. That page does not mention the concessionaire Angelo Ferrari; his winning of the tender on 11 March 1889 comes from Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 5, and is tagged reconstruction there.
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of May the first stone goes down on Cerrito, one block from the rooms where Meano has been living for six years. The theatre is a private concession won at public tender, and it is meant to open on the four hundredth anniversary of the landfall of Columbus, two years and five months away. Tamburini has drawn it. Meano has drawn on it, at the boards, in a way the finished credits will never separate out. The 1892 date is missed by sixteen years.
suggested_refs: Teatro Colon, Cerrito 628: cornerstone of 25 May 1890, intended for the Columbus quadricentennial
sources: Teatro Colon official history, teatrocolon.org.ar/el-teatro/
working/journeys/francesco_tamburini.journey.json (cornerstone stop, 1890-05-25)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the death of Tamburini
stops.date_confidence: contested. Contemporary biographical evidence and the atlas file for Tamburini give 4 December 1890; the Teatro Colon's own official history says 1891, and Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 5, also write 1891. The discrepancy is recorded here and not resolved. The quote is from Meano's Colon memoria of 1892.
stops.campa: Tamburini dies with the Colon at foundation level and the rest of his state work half drawn. Meano, six years a hand in that studio, inherits the sheets and the problem inside them. The theatre's own official history dates this death to 1891, a year late, and the archival study of Meano repeats the error. By his own later account the competition project had been a maximum scheme, made in haste, and its author was quietly reworking it when the illness came: a few months from the first symptom to the grave.
stops.quote: ...era solamente un proyecto de máxima, que se resentía demasiado de la precipitación con que había sido confeccionado... mientras Tamburini estaba estudiando las modificaciones que pensaba introducir a fin de que resultase un proyecto práctico y definitivo, le sobrevino la enfermedad que en pocos meses lo llevó a la tumba.
stops.quote_source: Vittorio Meano, memoria del proyecto del Teatro Colon (1892), quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 8
suggested_refs: Rodolfo Brandariz, El Colon de Francesco Tamburini, on the succession from Tamburini to Meano
sources: working/journeys/francesco_tamburini.journey.json (death stop)
Teatro Colon official history (giving 1891)
Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), pp. 5, 8

stops.name: Cerrito 628, the plans under his own signature
stops.date_confidence: attested: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 5, citing Andes 1892, for the definitive plans presented under Meano's signature; the Department of Public Works report approving the revision is dated 22 August 1892 in the same study and tagged reconstruction there. Month and day of the presentation are unknown and default to January.
stops.campa: He redraws the theatre. The central pavilion goes, the projections on the facade go, the whole building rises higher. The Department of Public Works approves the revision in August, and from this point the Colon is his to build. The argument over how much of the design is his begins in the same season and is still running in Argentina and in Italy. He signs the plans to take the responsibility before the critics, and writes in the same memoria that to Tamburini alone belongs the merit of the general idea of the project.
stops.quote: Presentamos con nuestra firma este trabajo para asumir completamente la responsabilidad ante la crítica; pero nos incumbe el deber de declarar, en reverente homenaje a la memoria de Tamburini, que a él solo pertenece el mérito de la idea general del proyecto.
stops.quote_source: Vittorio Meano, memoria del proyecto del Teatro Colon (1892), quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 8
suggested_refs: Meano's 1892 memoria for the Teatro Colon, the document in which he assigns the general idea to Tamburini
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), pp. 5, 8
working/journeys/francesco_tamburini.journey.json

stops.name: Cerrito 628, a genre that is not a style
stops.date_confidence: attested as text. The passage is printed twice in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), at printed pp. 7-8 and again at p. 26, and the second transcription settles the verb as 'llamamos', not 'llamaremos'; the underlying primary page is Meano's 1892 memoria, p. 6. The date used here is the DOP approval, an ordering device only.
stops.campa: In the memoria he states his method and refuses the word style for it, style being too mannered a thing to claim. Every later attack on his Congress will be aimed at the recipe he sets down here, in 1892, for a theatre. What he wants is the general character of the Italian Renaissance, alternating with the good distribution and solidity of detail proper to German architecture, and with the grace, variety and bizarreria of French ornament, three national tempers held inside one building by an Italian working in Argentina.
stops.quote: El género de arquitectura que hemos adoptado...que no llamamos estilo por ser demasiado manierato, quisiera tener los caracteres generales del Renacimiento Italiano, alternados con la buena distribución y solidez de detalle propia de la arquitectura alemana, y la gracia, variedad y bizarría de ornamentación, propia de la arquitectura francesa.
stops.quote_source: Vittorio Meano, memoria del proyecto del Teatro Colon (1892), p. 6, quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), printed pp. 7-8 and again p. 26
suggested_refs: The 1892 Colon memoria, printed in full extract in the 1997 IAA study
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), pp. 7-8, 26

stops.name: Cerrito 628, against Garnier on the question of sound
stops.date_confidence: attested as text, from Meano's 1892 Colon memoria quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 9. The month is an ordering device; the memoria carries only the year. Garnier's own position is summarized by Meano and was not checked here against Garnier's writings.
stops.campa: Charles Garnier had written that the acoustics of a theatre lie beyond calculation, a matter of luck no architect governs. Meano, a surveyor by training, will not have it. Sound diffuses and rebounds; diffusion and percussion are technical questions; technical questions come apart under the simplicity of scientific analysis. He does not claim an absolute solution, only one good enough to satisfy the public and the singers at once. The hall he is calculating will not open in his lifetime.
stops.quote: Nosotros no participamos de la opinión del célebre arquitecto [Garnier], porque muy habituados a considerar las cosas bajo su faz práctica y a descomponer las cuestiones técnicas con la sencillez del análisis científico, no dudamos en lo más mínimo de que los problemas de difusión y percusión de los sonidos en los teatros, tengan su solución, si no absoluta, por lo menos capaz de satisfacer las exigencias recíprocas del público y de los artistas.
stops.quote_source: Vittorio Meano, memoria del proyecto del Teatro Colon (1892), quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 9
suggested_refs: Charles Garnier, Le Theatre (1871), the acoustic scepticism Meano is answering
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 9

stops.name: Cerrito 628, the concession collapses
stops.date_confidence: attested: the Teatro Colon's official history records the insolvency of the concessionaire enterprise and the halt to construction in 1894. The transfer of the unfinished works to the Municipality by Law 3474 in 1897, after Angelo Ferrari's death, comes from Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 5, and is tagged reconstruction there. Month defaults to January.
stops.campa: Angelo Ferrari's company runs out of money and the site stops. Nothing has failed in the design; a private concession has simply exhausted itself against a hole in the ground on Cerrito. Ferrari dies, and in 1897 a law hands the whole unfinished enterprise over to the Municipality of Buenos Aires. Meano keeps the file for another decade with no working site under it. By then he has a second and much larger palace to raise, eight blocks west along the Avenida de Mayo.
suggested_refs: Law 3474 (1897), transferring the Teatro Colon works to the Municipality of Buenos Aires
sources: Teatro Colon official history, teatrocolon.org.ar/el-teatro/
Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 5

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the law that calls the competition
stops.date_confidence: attested: the official Argentine monument record (argentina.gob.ar) gives Law 3187 of 20 November 1894 authorizing the building, with a presidential decree the following February organizing the international competition.
stops.campa: A law of the twentieth of November authorizes a permanent house for a national legislature that has sat until now in borrowed rooms. A decree in February organizes an international competition for it. The ground chosen is the western end of the Avenida de Mayo, the avenue Juan Antonio Buschiazzo has just driven straight through the colonial centre, so that whatever rises here will close that axis and be read down its whole length from the government house.
suggested_refs: Law 3187 of 20 November 1894 and the presidential decree of February 1895 organizing the competition
sources: argentina.gob.ar, official monument record for the Congreso Nacional
working/journeys/juan_antonio_buschiazzo.journey.json (Avenida de Mayo inauguration stop, 1894-07-09)

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the memoria and the eternal book
stops.date_confidence: attested as text: Meano's 'Genesis del Congreso' (1895) is quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), pp. 24-26, from pp. 29 and 32 of the original. The month is an ordering device; the memoria carries only the year.
stops.campa: With the drawings he sends an argument. He will not take up Byzantine, Romanesque, Arab, Gothic, Renaissance, baroque or rococo. He goes to Roman magnificence and tempers its pomp with the purity of Greek line, not combining the two styles but taking from each what will carry the present. Behind the method sits a conviction about materials: architecture is the book in which peoples write with indelible letters, and a nation that builds in mortar rather than granite is writing itself a mean page.
stops.quote: Tampoco echaremos mano de las varias arquitecturas que han precedido a las modernas... llámense ellas bizantino, románico, árabe, gótico, renacimiento, barocco, rococó... Acudiremos pues a la magnificencia romana... procuraremos... templar la pompa y la ostentación romana con la pureza de las líneas griegas... pero no combinando los dos estilos, sino tomando de cada uno de ellos lo bastante para aprovechar sus caracteres más sobresalientes, más típicos, más aptos para amoldarse á las actuales exijencias y expresar más sinceramente el pensamiento moderno.
stops.quote_source: Vittorio Meano, 'Genesis del Congreso' (1895), quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 26
suggested_refs: Meano's printed album Edificio para Congreso Nacional and the memoria 'Genesis del Congreso' (1895)
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), pp. 24-26

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, first prize, unanimous
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the unanimity: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), pp. 8-9, citing Massini Correas 1965; argentina.gob.ar also dates the win to 1895, and the 12 October 1895 deadline comes from es.wikipedia. Conflict recorded: argentina.gob.ar's record reads 8 January 1896 as the award, which es.wikipedia identifies instead as approval of the work-direction contract, the contract itself following on 31 July 1896.
stops.campa: Twenty-eight or twenty-nine schemes come in; seventeen of the entrants have been identified since. The jury gives Meano first place by unanimity, with M. Turner second, and the commission records the decision in its seventh acta. He is thirty-five, an Italian geometra who has never built a building under his own name, and he has just been handed the largest public work in the country. The contract to direct the works is approved in January and signed the following July.
stops.quote: El palacio del Congreso se levantará pues en el lugar fijado, marcando con su fachada principal el 'non plus ultra' del trazado magestuoso de la Avenida de Mayo.
stops.quote_source: Vittorio Meano, 'Genesis del Congreso' (1895), p. 29, quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 25
suggested_refs: The seventh acta of the Congress competition commission, naming Meano the winner
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), pp. 8-9, 25
argentina.gob.ar, official monument record
es.wikipedia, 'Palacio del Congreso de la Nacion Argentina'

stops.name: Rodriguez Pena 30, the house that is also the office
stops.date_confidence: the address is attested by La Nacion (2019), which places it on Rodriguez Pena at 30, near Rivadavia. The 1895 death of Luigia's first husband, the legal marriage and the staff of about fifteen come only from the 1997 study through an unread PDF and are reconstruction. The date orders the segment. Coordinates corrected to Nominatim.
stops.campa: Her first husband dies in Italy and the two of them marry, eleven years after leaving as a fiction. They take a house on Rodriguez Pena, four blocks from the Congress ground, and the house becomes an office: an architect, engineers, draughtsmen, a photographer, some fifteen people on the payroll. The Buenos Aires papers call her Luisa now, and the palace going up down the street is expected to take four years. From the door he can reach the Congress ground in ten minutes on foot and the dead Colon site in twenty.
suggested_refs: Rodriguez Pena 30, near Rivadavia: the Meano house and studio, 1896-1904
sources: La Nacion, 'Cronicas del crimen: el asesinato de Vittorio Meano', 21 November 2019
Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997)

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, Besana takes the works
stops.date_confidence: contested on the month. Rita Molinos (2011) puts Pablo Besana y Hno. in charge from March 1897; es.wikipedia says the works began in August 1897; argentina.gob.ar says 1898. The contract figure is contested too: the 1997 study is reported at 5,776,545 pesos moneda nacional, es.wikipedia at 5,776,745. Neither figure is stated to the peso here.
stops.campa: Meano draws a new pre-project for the tender and the contract goes to Pablo Besana y Hno. for something over five and three quarter million pesos moneda nacional. The sources cannot agree what month the picks went in, and they cannot agree on the last three digits of the sum. The shape of the bargain is not in doubt. The price is fixed and the site is old riverbed, and the client is the legislature itself, which can vote at any hour of any session to change its mind about its own house.
suggested_refs: The Besana contract of 1897 for the Palacio del Congreso, and the pre-project Meano drew for the tender
sources: Rita Molinos, 'La piedra en el papel. La construccion del Palacio del Congreso Nacional', Anales del IAA 41, no. 1 (2011)
Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 13
es.wikipedia; argentina.gob.ar (both differing)

segments.name: The Stone and the Iron Circle

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the ground refuses the weight
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Luis A. Huergo's report on the foundation soil is dated 23 February 1897 in Molinos (2011). The count of roughly 1,500 piles and the names Massini and Duclout trace only to that article, whose full text was 403-locked to the gathering pass; argentina.gob.ar's monument record names no engineers and gives no pile count, contrary to the dossier's tagging.
stops.campa: The site is old riverbed. Luis Huergo reports on what the ground under the Plaza will and will not carry, and the answer sets the terms of everything after: something near fifteen hundred piles driven, an inverted vault of masonry spread beneath the dome to share the load out across mud. The dome is the heaviest object anyone has proposed to set on this soil, and the inverted vault that will carry it is buried out of sight before a single cornice is cut above it.
suggested_refs: Luis A. Huergo's soil report of 23 February 1897, submitted to the Dean of the Engineering Faculty
sources: Molinos, 'La piedra en el papel' (2011), note 9

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the decision to face it in stone
stops.date_confidence: attested: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 13, records that from 1898 an extended sequence of supplementary contracts follows from the decision to face the building in stone; Molinos (2011), pp. 159-160, covers Meano's decisions on the stone tender during the foundation-consolidation dispute of 1898-1899. Month defaults to January.
stops.campa: Congress decides that its own house will not be rendered in mortar but faced in cut stone, which is precisely what Meano had argued for in the memoria of 1895, and the price of the building begins to climb. From here the works proceed by supplementary contract, one after another, each legally separate and each adding to a figure the newspapers can print in a headline. He gets the granite he had asked for. The decision to spend on it is the legislature's own, and the overrun that follows is reported under his name.
suggested_refs: The supplementary contracts of 1898 onward for the stone facing of the Palacio del Congreso

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the scaffolds seen from the street
stops.date_confidence: attested that Caras y Caretas published a description of the half-risen building over the byline 'Fray Gerundio', cited in Molinos (2011). The dossier's identification of that byline with Jose Sixto Alvarez is rejected here: Alvarez signed himself Fray Mocho, and Fray Gerundio was a short-lived periodical he wrote for, not a pen name. The author of the piece is left unidentified.
stops.campa: A reporter for Caras y Caretas walks the works and writes what any passer-by can see: a half-risen mass inside a cage of timber, carts, a pit, and no palace. The piece is signed Fray Gerundio. Argentine memory keeps wanting that byline to belong to Jose Sixto Alvarez, the great chronicler of the city, but Alvarez signed himself Fray Mocho, and Fray Gerundio was the name of a paper rather than of a man. Who walked the works that January is not known.

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the Palace of Gold
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The judgment attributed to President Julio Argentino Roca, 'antiartistica, inadecuada y monstruosa', is reported in Molinos (2011), which the gathering pass could not open directly, and no primary transcript was located. The 1900 commission and its members are likewise reported there and not independently confirmed. The month orders the cost crisis of 1900.
stops.campa: The press names the building the Palace of Gold. From the government house at the other end of the avenue, Julio Argentino Roca, in his second presidency, is reported to have called the design unartistic, unsuitable and monstrous. That is the client speaking about a house he is legally obliged to pay for. The same year a commission including Ezequiel Ramos Mexia and Antonio Bermejo goes through the accounts and finds the conduct of Meano and of Besana in order, laying the overrun where it belongs, on the legislature's own decision to build in stone.

stops.name: Rodriguez Pena 30, the album of the theatres of the world
stops.date_confidence: the 1900 two-volume album is recorded in the bibliography through Molinos and Puppo; the 1900 originals were not located online. A 175-page facsimile circulating since 2019 was confirmed by page count alone on a document-sharing listing that names no compiler, publisher or ISBN, so the attribution of that facsimile to Molinos and Puppo is reconstruction. stops.campa: Out of the house on Rodriguez Pena comes a book in two volumes: El nuevo Teatro Colon y los principales teatros del mundo, his own unbuilt theatre set beside the plans and sections of the great houses of Europe, measured against them one by one. The Colon site has been dead for six years and will stay dead for three more. He publishes the comparison anyway, insisting by the act of it that the thing on Cerrito is a project and not a ruin. No copy of the original two volumes has been located since.

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, El Hormigon
stops.date_confidence: attested: Manuel Mayol's cover 'El Hormigon' ran in Caras y Caretas no. 106, 13 October 1900, cited in Molinos (2011). stops.campa: Manuel Mayol puts the Congress on the cover of Caras y Caretas as an anthill, hormigon being both the concrete and the swarm, the joke aimed at a swarm that eats money. A month later Law 3974 tries to put the disordered process back in order. Within the year the works are largely suspended for want of funds, and when they restart in 1903 the monthly certificates are capped and the Ministry of Public Works stands closer at the architect's shoulder than before.

stops.name: Rodriguez Pena 30, a second parliament under a motto
stops.date_confidence: contested on the calling of the competition. Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 11, date it to 1903 under President Jose Batlle y Ordonez; es.wikipedia gives an enabling law of 1902, when Juan Lindolfo Cuestas was still in office, with entries received through 1904. The severe Greek scheme and the Vienna Parliament model are reported by Tosoni (2019) and not independently confirmed.
stops.campa: Uruguay wants a legislative palace and calls the world to design one, anonymously, each entry under a motto. Meano, with one parliament stalled around him, draws a second. He takes the word Agraciada, the name of the avenue the building will face in Montevideo. This time there is no great dome. The scheme is severe and Greek where the Buenos Aires one is Roman and crowned, and what changed in the ten years between them may be his taste or may only be the budget he is handed. The model reported for it is the parliament house in Vienna.

stops.name: Rodriguez Pena 30, the transaction with the ideals
stops.date_confidence: attested as text: the passage is quoted from p. 26 of Meano's 1904 memoria for the Montevideo palace in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 14. The month is an ordering device; the memoria carries only the year.
stops.campa: Writing the memoria that will go in the envelope with the drawings, he allows himself one confession. He is satisfied with the architecture. He is not satisfied with the arrangement, the transaction he has had to make with his own ideals in submitting them to a budget. He is forty-three and has been building with other people's money for twelve years, and the envelope will go across the river unsigned, carrying nothing but a word. We have not done it without violence, he writes; permit us to say so.
stops.quote: ...si nos atrevemos a confesar cierta satisfacción por el resultado de nuestra concepción arquitectónica, mentiríamos si dijéramos que nos satisface también ese arreglo, esa transacción que hemos debido hacer con nuestros ideales, sometiéndolos a las exigencias del presupuesto; no lo hemos hecho sin violencia, permítase que lo manifestemos.
stops.quote_source: Vittorio Meano, memoria del proyecto para el Palacio Legislativo de Montevideo (1904), p. 26, quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 14

stops.name: Montevideo, the twenty-seven envelopes
stops.date_confidence: attested: twenty-seven entries and the April 1904 deadline are confirmed by es.wikipedia and by Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 12. The ship image is Meano's own words, but only inside the quotation marks: 'Habria sido' is the 1997 study's framing, and it cites Meano 1904, p. 27. Contradiction recorded: the same corpus also places a similar remark in a private letter of May 1900 about the Argentine Congress. Coordinates corrected to the building per Nominatim.
stops.campa: Twenty-seven sealed schemes reach Montevideo by the fifteenth of April. No name appears on any of them; the jury judges mottoes and opens the envelopes afterward. Among them is Agraciada, sent across the river from a drawing office in Buenos Aires by a man who has never stood on the site and never will. In the memoria he had said what the building would have been had he been left the room to build it whole: a great ship navigating anxiously between the narrow banks of a small river.
stops.quote: un gran buque navegando angustiosamente entre las estrechas orillas de un pequeño río
stops.quote_source: Vittorio Meano, memoria del proyecto para el Palacio Legislativo de Montevideo (1904), p. 27, quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 14

stops.name: Rodriguez Pena 30, five minutes before ten
stops.date_confidence: attested in outline: contemporary witness testimony in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 15, with La Nacion (2019) and Infobae (2020) for the address and sequence, and Juan Forn (Pagina/12, 2009) independently confirming the date, the former servant and the two shots. Forn places the encounter in a bedroom, which sits awkwardly against the denial of the 'caught in bed' tableau. The killer's forename is unsettled across sources as Carlo, Carlos M. or Juan Passera, and his age as 25 or 28. The limp, the cane, the door frame and the left lung are unverified; the dying exclamation is press reconstruction.
stops.campa: He comes back from the works at about five minutes before ten and finds his former manservant inside the house. Words, then the man goes up the stairs and Meano after him, then two shots: one into a door frame, one into his chest. He is dead within minutes. The house is full of people, an office of fifteen at work downstairs, and nobody gets between the two men in time. What the papers report him calling out is not a curse and not a name: they have killed me, embalm my body.
stops.quote: ¡Me han muerto, que embalsamen mi cadáver!
stops.quote_source: Attributed last words of Vittorio Meano, 1 June 1904, quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 15, citing period press coverage
suggested_refs: Mario Sabugo, 'Quien mato a Vittorio Meano?', Summa+ no. 4 (December 1993), republished at cafedelasciudades.com.ar
sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 15

stops.name: Comisaria 7a, the case is opened
stops.date_confidence: attested that the Seventh Precinct under Enrique Quintana ran the investigation and that Passera surrendered to the investigating judge Constanzo within hours, per La Nacion (2019); accounts differ on whether the surrender came late the same day or the following morning. The seventeen-year sentence is reported by the same article. The precinct's exact address was not established and the pin is approximate.
stops.campa: Patrolman Domingo Nogueira reaches the house first. The killer has already gone out through an adjoining property onto Rivadavia, and the Seventh Precinct under Enrique Quintana issues an order of capture it turns out not to need: within hours the man has seen a lawyer and given himself up to the investigating judge, pleading self-defence against an architect who walked with a cane. The court will convict him and sentence him to seventeen years' imprisonment.

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta, three in the afternoon
stops.date_confidence: attested: the burial at the Cementerio del Norte is in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 15, and Juan Forn (Pagina/12, 2009) independently confirms the vault of the Botto and Solari families, Genoese friends from the crossing and founders of the Hospital Italiano. Whether the remains are still there, and whether the vault is marked, no reachable source says. Coordinates corrected to Nominatim; the dossier's two lenses had disagreed on the hemisphere.
stops.campa: The cortege leaves the house at three and the Sociedad Central de Arquitectos calls its members out to walk behind it. He has no tomb of his own in this city and no family in it either, so he goes into the vault of two Genoese friends from the crossing over, Giuseppe Solari and Pellegrino Botto. Alejandro Christophersen, presiding over the architects, speaks at the graveside about his personal virtues. An unsigned notice in the same month's Revista Tecnica says instead that Meano lacked the gift of assimilation a man needs who resigns himself to carrying his pilgrim ground to another country.
stops.quote: ...Meano carecía de ese don de asimilación indispensable al hombre que se resigna a trasladar su tierra de peregrino a otras tierras que la natal...
stops.quote_source: "Ch", 'Victor Meano', Revista Tecnica - Arquitectura, ano I, n. 4 (Buenos Aires, 1904), quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), printed p. 4. The study distinguishes this byline from Christophersen's own signed graveside address.

stops.name: Rodriguez Pena 30, the letters in the servant's room
stops.date_confidence: attested: Caras y Caretas (1904), cited in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 15, for the search and the letters, and La Nacion (2019) for the widow's questioning at the house and her brief detention. The closure of the instruction on 10 June, charging Passera with homicide and the widow with concealment, is reported in the 1997 study and tagged reconstruction there. La Nacion reports her later exoneration and return to Italy.
stops.campa: Police open the killer's lodging and carry out love letters addressed to the widow, a wardrobe of clothes, and prescriptions from a dentist. On the eighth they question her in her own house, with the drawings of two parliaments still on the tables. The instruction closes on the tenth: homicide against him, concealment against her. Caras y Caretas prints the inventory for its readers. She is exonerated in the end and goes back to Italy. No court ever established why Passera fired.

stops.name: Montevideo, Agraciada is chosen
stops.date_confidence: attested in substance by es.wikipedia and by Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), pp. 11-12: the advisory jury under engineer Juan Alberto Capurro left first prize vacant, ranked 'Hispania' second and 'Agraciada' third, and the governing Palacio Commission then judged Meano's the more executable scheme and voted to build it. es.wikipedia states he was murdered before he could be contacted. Month is an ordering device.
stops.campa: The jury in Montevideo declines to award a first prize at all. It puts Manuel Mendoza y Saez's Hispania second and Agraciada third. Then the commission that actually has to raise the building reads the drawings again, decides Agraciada is the one that can be built for the money available, and votes for it subject to modification. Then the envelope with the motto on it is opened. The name inside belongs to a man who was shot dead in his own hallway three months ago, across the river, in a country the jury has no business with.

stops.name: Rodriguez Pena 30, the second shooting
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997) name the second servant as Gaspar Pecchio and place the attack weeks after the murder; La Nacion (2019) dates it roughly three months after and gives no name. Both agree the widow was shot in the arm and the man then killed himself on or near the bed. The month is a compromise between the two accounts.
stops.campa: Another dismissed servant of the same household comes back, shoots the widow through the arm, and then kills himself on the bed. One account names him Gaspar Pecchio, another gives no name at all, and they differ by weeks on when he came. Three months, two guns, one address. She survives the arm wound and does not stay in the country much longer. What was going on inside that house? No court established it, no source since has established it, and the erotic explanation Buenos Aires settled on rests on nothing anybody can produce.
suggested_refs: Mario Sabugo, Vittorio Meano: la vida, la obra, la fama, annex 3, 'El movil de Passera'

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, opened unfinished
stops.date_confidence: attested: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 13, gives 12 May 1906 for the inauguration by President Figueroa Alcorta, and argentina.gob.ar records the partial inauguration with works continuing. The building was declared complete only in 1946.
stops.campa: Two years after the murder, President Figueroa Alcorta opens the Palacio del Congreso. The dome is up and the chambers can sit and the building is nowhere near finished. The decoration is incomplete, the stone facing of the western front is forty years from done, and the works will go on that whole time, under Jules Dormal and then under whoever came after him. The legislature takes possession of a construction site with a roof on it and begins passing laws inside.

sources: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (1997), p. 13

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the commissions of 1907 and 1914
stops.date_confidence: attested that two investigating commissions sat in 1907 and 1914, with Alfredo Palacios, Jorge Newbery and Lisandro de la Torre among their members, per Juan Forn (Pagina/12, 2009); they examined the construction's finances, not the murder. Forn also reports de la Torre pursuing the question of whether Meano had been removed as an obstacle, and finding nothing. Correction recorded: the 'cursed architects' framing is Forn writing in retrospect in 2009, not a contemporaneous press campaign, since Julian Garcia Nunez died in 1944 and Arturo Prins belongs to the same later period. Month defaults to January.
stops.campa: Twice the Congress investigates its own building. Alfredo Palacios, Jorge Newbery and Lisandro de la Torre sit on those commissions, and what they are after is where the money went. De la Torre pushes further and asks whether the architect was killed to clear an obstacle out of the way of the accounts. He turns up nothing, and the theory outlives him. The story that groups Meano with other doomed architects of the city is written later still, in 2009, by a columnist looking back.

sources: Juan Forn, 'Congreso (autor anonimo)', Pagina/12, 3 April 2009

stops.name: Cerrito 628, Aida
stops.date_confidence: attested: the Teatro Colon's official history gives 25 May 1908 and Verdi's Aida, and records the Salon Dorado and the iron marquees on Libertad and Cerrito as unfinished at the inauguration. The completion under Jules Dormal is stated in the same source and in the atlas file for Tamburini, which describes a changed structure and a heavier French finish.
stops.campa: Eighteen years after the cornerstone the theatre opens with Aida, on the anniversary of the day the first stone went down. Francesco Tamburini began it, Meano redrew and signed it, Jules Dormal finished it with a heavier French hand than either Italian would have used. The Salon Dorado is not done. The iron marquees on Libertad and Cerrito are not up. The acoustics Meano had insisted could be calculated turn out to have been calculated correctly.

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the egg in the egg cup
stops.date_confidence: attested as quoted text, through a chain: Jules Huret (1910) and Anatole France (1909, via Buschiazzo 1966) are both quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), pp. 16-17. The study itself flags the France attribution chain as uncertain and no French original was located; Mario Sabugo's essay repeats the France line without a dated citation. Month defaults to January.
stops.campa: Visiting Europeans look up the avenue and write home. Anatole France calls the palace an Italian salad of Greek, Roman and French ingredients: the colonnade of the Louvre, with the Parthenon set inside it, and the Pantheon set on top of that, and the whole cake dusted over with allegories, statues, balustrades and terraces, like the confusion at Babel. Jules Huret is briefer. A colossal egg in an egg cup, twelve million francs budgeted and fifty-five spent, and still not finished.
stops.quote: En el otro extremo de la Avenida de Mayo se levanta el monumento del congreso cuya cúpula algo delgada produce el efecto de un huevo colosal colocado sobre una huevera... Este edificio, proyectado hace muchos años, con un presupuesto de 12 millones de francos, ha absorbido hasta hoy 55 millones. ¡Y aún no está concluido!... Ha costado tanto dinero que se llama la 'Casa de Oro'.
stops.quote_source: Jules Huret (1910), quoted in Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo, Vittorio Meano (IAA-FADU-UBA, 1997), p. 16

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the last facing stones
stops.date_confidence: attested: Baeza, Molinos and Sabugo (1997), p. 13, and the official Argentine monument record both give 1946 for the completion of the stone facings on the western facade, closing a construction begun in 1897-1898. Month defaults to January.
stops.campa: The stone facing on the western front is finished in 1946. Forty-two years after the architect was shot in his own hallway, and half a century after the first pile went into the mud, the building is called complete. Everyone who signed the original contract is dead. The granite pages he had argued for in 1895 are all in place, and the sum they cost has stopped being a scandal and become a line in a monument record. No full accounting of the whole works has ever been published in one place.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the city that named nothing after him
stops.date_confidence: negative finding, stated as a gap: no Buenos Aires monument, plaque or renamed street to Meano was found in any source reached. The Digitalia catalogue record for the standard biography, fetched directly, gives Mario Sabugo, Nobuko, 2011, 114 pages, in three parts with an annex on Passera's motive; a 2004 first edition was not confirmed, and es.wikipedia credits the same title to Rita Molinos, so the authorship is unsettled across three attributions.
stops.campa: Two of the largest buildings in Buenos Aires are his, and there is no street, plaza or plaque in the city with his name on it. What there is instead is a literature. Mario Sabugo asks in print who killed Vittorio Meano, calls him a Nimrod of Piedmont, and reads the dome against the tower of Babel. The standard biography comes in three parts, La Vida, La Obra, La Fama, and closes with an annex titled the motive of Passera. Even its own authorship is disputed, credited to Sabugo in one catalogue and to Rita Molinos in another.

stops.name: Montevideo, a plazoleta with his name on it
stops.date_confidence: attested: Intendencia de Montevideo Resolucion 1363/19 of 18 March 2019 was fetched directly and matches in every element, including the three bounding streets and the wording of the marker. The pin is the approximate intersection of Colombia and Francisco de Paula Marti; the resolution gives no coordinates.
stops.campa: Montevideo names a small triangle of public ground for him, bounded by Colombia, Francisco de Paula Marti and the Avenida Agraciada, the avenue whose name he had used as his motto in 1904. The resolution that creates it is numbered 1363 and dated the eighteenth of March. It is the only ground anywhere that carries his name, and it lies in a country he never entered, beside a building he never saw begun. The marker reads: ARQ. stops.name: Frossasco, the museum of the emigration
stops.date_confidence: attested: the Museo Regionale dell'Emigrazione dei Piemontesi nel Mondo, Piazza Donatori di Sangue 1, Frossasco, presents Meano among its leading emigrant professionals (museoemigrazionepiemontese.it, fetched directly). stops.campa: Forty kilometres from Gravere, in a small town on the edge of the plain, Piedmont keeps a museum of the people it exported. Meano is in it, among the masons and the hotelkeepers and the engineers, listed as one of the region's leading professionals abroad. The same institution says he did his technical schooling in Turin, which is not what the Argentine literature says, and the two accounts of one boyhood have never been laid side by side by anyone able to settle them.
